text: Francis Cornford wrote that the artistic design of this work was like "a set of volcanic islands [heaving] themselves out of the sea." This work "is an everlasting possession, not a prize composition which is heard and forgotten," according to its translation by the 19th-century Master of Balliol, Benjamin Jowett. Its final sections contain the text of three treaties with Tissaphernes. Early in this work, a group of exiled nobles join the Taulantians, an Illyrian tribe who lived around the colony of Epidamnus. The resulting dispute over Epidamnus between the cities of Corcyra and Corinth was a principle cause of this work's title event. Debate exists over the historicity of this work's speeches, of which the only epideictic example is the funeral oration delivered by Pericles.
